title: Seamless version handshake and state bridge for Private upgrades
creator: Samir Patel
description: Build a lightweight "handshake" protocol and transient state bridge that enables zero-to-minimal-downtime version rollouts for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) across cohorts. The feature covers coordinated version negotiation, ephemeral state transfer for KV and metadata, preflight compatibility checks, and deterministic cutover points tied to rollout gates. Goal: reduce manual migration steps and rollback surface for customers running multi-node Private clusters.
acceptance_criteria: New handshake API implemented and backward-compatible with 1.x agents
Can perform controlled canary cohort upgrade with automatic state bridge and no more than 3s median additional tail latency during quiesce window
Automated preflight reports for schema/manifest mismatches surfaced in Console and upgrade runbook
Successful end-to-end test: orchestrated upgrade of a 3-node VPC cluster with transactional writes preserved and automatic rollback upon parity-check failure
Runbook and operator CLI documented; example GitHub PR with rollout policy attached
implementation_notes: Design handshake as short-lived gRPC session between old and new control-plane agents; session establishes feature flags, manifest versions, and a deterministic cutover epoch
Introduce ephemeral state bridge service that streams KV diffs and schema migrations in order. Use write-order tokens to guarantee idempotency across retries
Backward compatibility: agents that don't implement handshake fall back to conservative drain-and-upgrade flow (existing path)
Use a two-phase preflight: local (node-level) compatibility checks followed by cluster-wide dry-run using replica snapshots
Keep binary-level changes minimal in control-plane; complex transform logic lives in migration transformers registered as plug-ins
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag gated rollout to internal staging (5% of internal infra); validate telemetry and error modes
Phase 1: Canary cohort - single-customer non-critical workload in dedicated sandbox cluster
Phase 2: Beta - invited customers on Dedicated for guided migration workshops
Phase 3: Gradual GA by region and account size; default remains conservative drain unless customer opts into handshake
Each phase requires: successful preflight on 3 consecutive runs, <1% upgrade failure rate, and no unresolved security review items
rollback_plan: Automatic abort if post-cutover parity checks fail within 10 minutes
On abort: revert traffic routing, replay write-order tokens to roll forward or restore from ephemeral bridge snapshot depending on divergence
Provide a safe manual rollback command in CLI that can pin cluster to previous version and trigger a reconciliation run
Document timeouts and operator remediation steps in runbook with example logs and CLI commands
test_plan: Unit tests for handshake negotiation state machine and idempotency semantics
Integration tests: 3-node and 7-node Private cluster upgrades using chaos (network partitions, delayed KV apply)
E2E tests that validate application-visible consistency for typical LLM workloads (server-side session KV, inference cache)
Performance tests: measure median and 95th percentile token-serving latency during quiesce windows across instance sizes
Security tests: verify handshake cannot be replayed or spoofed; KMS-protected tokens rotate per-session
telemetry: Ephemeral-bridge bytes transferred and applied per-migration
Parity check results and divergence vectors
Upgrade gate metrics to show how many customers auto-accepted vs. manual intervention
risks: State bridge complexity may expose edge cases for custom on-prem storage layouts
Mis-specified transformers could cause data drift if preflight misses schema behavior
Network flakiness during bridge streaming can increase window for quiesce and affect latency SLOs
Customers running heavy transactional loads may prefer full drain; handshake could give false confidence if not properly gated
comments: 2025-01-28 Samir Patel: Initial ticket created. Spike completed on proof-of-concept: two agents can negotiate versions and stream a small KV delta reliably over gRPC.
2025-02-05 Marina Olsson: Design review done with infra and security. Decided to use per-session ephemeral tokens minted by control-plane KMS. Security review pre-check added to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-12 Eng Architect (Lena Morris): Proposed deterministic cutover epoch implemented as monotonic 'epoch token' embedded in write-order. Agreed to keep transformer plugin API stable across v1 and v2 agents.

2025-02-20 QA (Diego Ramos): Integration harness for simulated network partitions landed in test infra. Found race where repeated reconnects could cause duplicate application of diffs; introduced idempotency via write-order check.
2025-02-28 Marina Olsson: Implemented first-pass CLI for manual inspect and abort. Added telemetry hooks for handshake latency and failure reasons.
2025-03-03 Security (Aisha Kapoor): Reviewed threat model. Minor changes requested: tighten replay window and rotate ephemeral tokens more frequently. Patch merged in PR #1423.

2025-03-10 Samir Patel: Began phased rollout to staging. Initial telemetry shows 0.8% handshake transient failures (expected due to flaky test nodes). Next action: decrease reconnect jitter and improve backoff handling.
